newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain electric protocol sets 2 trln pta sunk costs.
newsitem.headline: Spain electric protocol sets 2 trln pta sunk costs.

text.p: Guidelines setting out a new regime for Spain's electricity sector recognise total sunk costs of almost two trillion pesetas, Industry Minister Josep Pique reaffirmed on Wednesday.
The document known as the electricity protocol is due to be signed by sector companies and the government either today or tomorrow, Pique told a senate committee.
The protocol will be a step towards introducing more competition in this heavily-regulated sector.
"In the end, the figure (for sunk costs) taken into account globally will be almost 2 trillion pesetas," he said.
Sunk, or stranded costs, are fixed costs in plant and generation which in general will no longer be compensated by the state under the new more competitive regime.
The two trillion pesetas figure includes 300 billion pesetas incentives to prompt demand for coal, for which a one peseta per kilowatt premium will be paid, Pique said.
A further 200 billion pesetas will correspond to compensation for extraordinary investments.
All in all, "costs recognised (in the protocol) to adapt to competition will be 1.5 trillion pesetas," the minister said.

Pique added that 80 percent of these costs would be divided among electricity companies, with the other 20 percent being allocated according to the results of work groups to be set up to study the issue.
